question: The Health Assessment Questionnaire Disability Index (HAQ-DI) is a validated patient-reported outcome measure (PROM) used to assess functional disability and quality of life in patients with rheumatoid arthritis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. The HAQ-DI is a well-validated PROM for RA, measuring functional disability across eight domains of daily living. It is used both clinically (to guide management) and in research (as a trial endpoint). Other PROMs used in RA include PROMIS and MDHAQ.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The HAQ-DI is one of the most widely used and validated PROMs in RA, assessing functional disability across eight domains: dressing, arising, eating, walking, hygiene, reach, grip, and activities. Scores range from 0 (no disability) to 3 (complete disability); a score >1.0 indicates moderate-to-severe functional limitation.
